title: TradingView Basics
hook: Your chart is your workspace. Learn it before you try to read it.

launchpad.outcome: Set up a clean, readable chart instead of a cluttered one.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Does adding more drawing tools to a chart make it easier to read, or harder?

slides.kicker: Your workspace, not a decoration contest
slides.body:
You're using TradingView to read price, change your perspective with timeframes, and mark behavior so your eyes stop feeling lost.

A horizontal level marking a repeated reaction area is one of the cleanest beginner tools, you don't need every feature to read a chart well.

check.prompt: A new trader adds ten different drawing tools to her chart at once, hoping more markings will make her read clearer.

options.label: Nothing, more tools always means a better read
options.feedback: More markings isn't automatically more useful information.

options.label: An overloaded chart makes price harder to read, not easier
options.why: Right. Clutter competes with price for your attention.

slides.quote: You do not need every feature. A few tools used clearly is better than a messy chart.

slides.body: Switching timeframes changes what you're looking at, not what's actually happening in the market underneath it.

check.prompt: Switching timeframes changes your ___ on the same market, not the market itself.

options.label: Instrument
options.feedback: The instrument doesn't change just because you zoomed in or out.

options.label: Perspective
options.why: Zooming in or out just changes what detail you can see, not the underlying price story.

options.label: Broker
options.feedback: Your broker has nothing to do with which timeframe you're viewing.

items.label: Read
items.desc: Your chart's job is showing you what price is doing.

items.label: Zoom
items.desc: Timeframes change your perspective, not the market.

items.label: Mark
items.desc: A few clean levels beat ten drawing tools.

items.label: Simplify
items.desc: If it doesn't help you read price, take it off the chart.

slides.prompt: Imagine another AGHF member asks: "Why does my chart look so messy compared to yours?" How would you explain it to them?
slides.modelAnswer: More drawing tools doesn't mean more clarity, usually it means more clutter. A clean chart uses a few tools clearly, like a couple of horizontal levels marking areas price has reacted to before, so your eyes can find the story instead of fighting through noise.

takeaways: TradingView is a workspace for reading price, not a decoration contest.
A cluttered chart makes price harder to read, not easier.
Switching timeframes changes your view, not the market itself.
remember: A few tools used clearly beats a messy chart.
